proposal.reasoning:
MARKERS AND OWNERSHIP. I searched the whole leaf for a maru-marker (circle + name + 藩) and there is none: no ○ glyph appears anywhere between x=420 and x=2280. The page is therefore wholly interior to one domain's block, and the only naming on the leaf is the running header at the far right, 藩制一覽表第一（出石）, which is provenance (fascicle 1, Izushi). MASTER independently assigns the page to 出石藩. Every box below is owned by 出石藩; the right-of-marker / left-of-marker rule never fires here, and there are no neighbour domains to attribute.

TWO TOP-RULE GROUP NOTES. Two bracketed labels sit on the horizontal rule at y≈1031–1094, printed rotated 180° relative to the body text. Rotating them upright they read （十月調） at x 1890–2093 (right) and （十一月調） at x 505–741 (left); ink-projection confirms the left one carries an extra 8-px vertical stroke (一) between 十 and 月 that the right one has no room for (十 at 2017–2061 abuts 月 at 1964–2010). The rule hooks downward at x≈950–1030, so the tenth-month note governs the tax columns to its right (込高 through 銀) and the eleventh-month note governs the household/population columns to its left.

COLUMN WALK, RIGHT TO LEFT (native x):
2213–2275 running header 藩制一覽表第一（出石）; 2182–2233 printed page number 二十八 at the bottom margin.
2055–2172 a warichu label split 5+3 — right line 込高新田高, left line 改出高 — over 貳千八百拾八石六斗四升四勺五才 (石6斗4升[合 skipped]4勺5才 = 2,818.64045).
1918–2031 正租 with a parenthesised warichu period note, right line 安政六己未年, left line 文久三癸亥年, then 五ヶ年平均.
1786–1873 米 壹萬貳千九百拾壹石六斗五升五合八才 = 12,911.65508 (18 glyph runs counted; 六 at 2206–2258 splits into two runs).
1661–1744 大豆 千六百八拾七石五斗壹合貳勺 = 1,687.5012.
1518–1611 合 壹萬四千五百九拾九石壹斗五升六合貳勺八才 = 14,599.15628 (21 glyph runs).
1413–1485 雜税 heading. 1253–1343 米 四百六拾七石壹斗壹升五合六勺四才 = 467.11564. 1133–1215 大豆 拾石五斗貳升三合五勺 = 10.5235. 994–1085 銀 五拾四貫五百九拾貳匁七分七厘, with a two-line warichu below at 970–1076 (right line 金一兩ニ付銀, left line 百匁之相場).
956–1007 （町在） qualifying 戸數 at 875–953 (七千七拾六軒 = 7,076). 815–869 （町在） qualifying 人口 at 734–811 (三萬二千二百壹人 = 32,201), with 內 at y 2107–2168 and the M/F split below at 699–814.
604–682 番人戸數 四拾貳軒 and 番人人口 百九拾七人 with its own 內 split. 455–560 （茶筅） 四十二軒 and 人口百九十二人 with its own 內 split, both numbers parenthesised.

ARITHMETIC NET — all four groups reconcile.
正租: 12,911.65508 + 1,687.5012 = 14,599.15628, exactly the printed 合. 人口: 16,286 + 15,915 = 32,201. 番人: 105 + 92 = 197. 茶筅: 86 + 106 = 192.

MASTER DISAGREEMENT — I TRUST THE SCAN. MASTER carries 出石藩 大豆 = 千六百八拾七石五斗壹升五合貳勺 (1,687.5152). Row-projection over x 1655–1750 finds exactly 15 glyph runs in that column (大豆 + 13 value glyphs), not 17, and a single-character crop at 5× of y 2100–2530 shows 斗 → 壹 → 合 → 貳 → 勺 with no 升 and no second 五. The correct reading is 千六百八拾七石五斗壹合貳勺 = 1,687.5012. The printed total settles it: 12,911.65508 + 1,687.5012 = 14,599.15628 matches the printed 合 to the last digit, whereas MASTER's 1,687.5152 would give 14,599.17028. MASTER has a phantom 「升五」 inserted; the page does not.

GEOMETRY. Every box was set from an ink projection (px<120) of its own region with ~7 px padding, then checked on a full-page overlay twice. 28 boxes, zero pairwise overlaps. The three M/F pairs share one top at the 男/女 glyph row and split at the measured mid-line of the merged sub-column run (人口 at x 756/757, 番人 at 604/605, 茶筅 at 478/479); the sub-columns touch with no white gap in the source, so a mid-line split is the best available cut. The structural 內 markers are deliberately left unboxed. The horizontal rules themselves are left unboxed; only the two bracketed month notes on them are annotated.

proposal.page_summary_en: This leaf is the fascicle-one entry for Izushi domain (出石藩) in Tajima, printed on book page 28. It records an included yield (込高) of 2,818.64045 koku from new fields and reassessment; a regular land tax (正租) averaged over the five years Ansei 6 (1859) to Bunkyū 3 (1863) of 12,911.65508 koku of rice and 1,687.5012 koku of soybeans, whose printed total 14,599.15628 koku reconciles exactly; and miscellaneous taxes (雜税) of 467.11564 koku of rice, 10.5235 koku of soybeans, and 54 kan 592 monme 7 fun 7 rin of silver, reckoned at the rate of 100 monme of silver to one ryō of gold. The demographic block gives 7,076 households and 32,201 people (16,286 male, 15,915 female) for town and countryside together, and then counts two occupational groups separately: 42 watchman (番人) households with 197 people, and 42 tea-whisk-maker (茶筅) households with 192 people. Rules across the head of the page date the tax columns to a tenth-month return and the household and population columns to an eleventh-month return.

proposal.page_summary_en: This leaf closes the fascicle-1 civil register of Hakata domain (伯太藩), a 13,500-koku Watanabe holding in Izumi province whose block opened on the facing earlier page. It records a miscellaneous tax in gold of 43 ryō 1 bu 3 shu plus 53.18 mon in ei-cash, its rice equivalent of 5.4363 koku, and a combined current-rice total (合現石) of 6,073.2917 koku, against 2,109 households and a population of 10,439. Below the commoner figures the page breaks out the non-commoner groups: 149 samurai and sotsu households (86 shizoku, 63 sotsu) holding 615 people, an outcast (穢多) group of 71 households and 294 people split evenly at 147 men and 147 women, 82 shrines with 8 shrine-attendant households and 22 people, 76 temples with 131 people, and 75 villages. The last column belongs to the next domain: the ○林田藩 marker opens Hayashida's block with an assessed yield (草高) of 14,889.6719 koku. Two totals do not close as printed — the male-plus-female split of the population falls 294 short of the printed 10,439 (exactly the outcast count), and the status breakdown of the 615 samurai-class people sums to 574.

proposal.reasoning:
SCAN: 3095x4551 px; paper block x≈330-2640, y≈280-4310. An ink projection over that block (threshold px<120, gap>25) resolves 15 vertical runs; discarding the paper-edge darkening at x 2576-2640 leaves 14 real columns. Reading RIGHT to LEFT (HI is vertical, rightmost column first):

(1) x 2154-2211 — outer right margin. Two separate y-runs: y 1390-1945 = the running head 藩制一覧表第一（新見）, and y 3229-3370 = the printed book-page number 六十四 (=64). Both are page furniture, not data. The running head is PROVENANCE: it names 新見 because 新見藩's block opens on this leaf; it does not mean every column here is Niimi's.

(2) x 1994-2094, y 1131-3058 — 寺院　五十九寺（僧六十二人　外ニ　山伏五戸　五人）. The opening paren prints as a wide arc over 僧; the closing arc sits under the final 人 at y≈3040-3058. 外ニ is small type, right-offset.

(3) x 1893-1965, y 1129-2019 — 兵隊　二小隊　六十名一小隊 (the six-glyph tail in small type).

(4) x 1741-1830, y 1468-2009 — the MARU-MARKER: ○ (1468-1547), 新 (1577-1657), 見 (1755-1834), 藩 (1927-2010). This is the only marker on the leaf.

DOMAIN BOUNDARY. The right-to-left rule puts everything RIGHT of the ○新見藩 marker with the PREVIOUS domain and everything LEFT of it with 新見藩. So columns (2) 寺院 and (3) 兵隊 are the tail of the preceding domain's fascicle-1 block, which in fascicle 1 ends on 寺院 then 兵隊 — exactly the ordering seen here. The preceding domain is 庭瀬藩 (Niwase, Bitchū): MASTER carries 庭瀬藩's fascicle-1 草高 on pdf_page 44, immediately before this leaf, and 新谷藩/西大路藩 come after. Independent confirmation from the dataset: MASTER's fascicle-8 military row for 庭瀬藩 reads 「二小隊　一小隊六十人」 = 120 men, which is the same force as the 兵隊 column here (二小隊, 六十名一小隊); 新見藩's own military is quite different (常備兵隊 75人 / 豫備歩兵 60人 / 豫備砲兵 19人). So the 寺院 and 兵隊 boxes are owned by 庭瀬藩, and the header column plus book-page number are page furniture assigned to the leaf's primary domain, 新見藩.

(5) x 1607-1697, y 1126-2619 — 草高　壹萬八千百九十六石一斗四升二勺. Fifteen glyph runs after the two label glyphs; 八 verified splayed-and-separate (not 人/入), 千 verified with the slanted stroke on top (not 十), 六 verified with its top lid. = 18,196.1402 koku. Matches MASTER exactly.

(6) x 1476-1577, y 1291-2721 — a two-line warichu label (right line 込高, left line 新田) over 百九十六石一斗四升二勺, closing with small 五年平均. = 196.1402 koku, five-year average.

ARITHMETIC NET #1: 18,196.1402 − 196.1402 = 18,000.0000 exactly, i.e. the domain's nominal 18,000-koku assessment plus a 196.1402-koku increment. The 込高新田 reading is therefore confirmed by the subtraction.

(7) x 1331-1427, y 1210-2703 — 正租米　五千七百三十一石四斗九升九勺 = 5,731.4909 koku (合 place skipped; sub-units strictly descending 石>斗>升>勺).

(8) x 1192-1287, y 1374-3032 — 金　二千二百四兩二分一朱ト永三十二文五分.

(9) x 1066-1153, y 1460-2803 — small-type 此米　四百四十石九斗一升九合, closing with small 石五兩立. Read AFTER the 金 column, so it converts the cash half of the land tax, not the rice half.

ARITHMETIC NET #2: 2,204兩 + 2分 (0.5) + 1朱 (0.0625) + 永32文5分 (0.0325 兩 at 1,000 文永 = 1 兩) = 2,204.595 兩. Divided by the stated 5 兩 per koku = 440.919 koku, which is exactly 四百四十石九斗一升九合. The 金 reading, the 此米 reading and the 石五兩立 rate all reconcile to the fourth decimal.

(10) x 934-1027, y 1203-2698 — 雜税米　二百九十六石七斗四升五合四勺 = 296.7454 koku.

(11) x 803-891, y 1360-2943 — 金　二百九十一兩一分三朱ト永十九文四分 = 291.4569 兩.

(12) x 666-774, y 1367-2328 — 金　五拾八兩 followed by a two-line warichu: right line 但年々不同, left line 鑪鍛冶牛馬市等. The first warichu glyph is 金-radical with a right component whose lower half is a solid wide box (皿, giving 盧) rather than the scattered 心 of 慮, so I read 鑪 (tatara ironworks) — the expected levy for a Bitchū mountain domain. At this scan resolution that single glyph is the least certain reading on the page.

(13) x 555-636, y 1115-1930 — 士族戸數　百二十四戸; then x 537-612, y 2037-2771 — 人口　五百九十二人; then the M/F warichu, one shared top at y≈2790, split by an ink valley at x 563/564: 男三百十二人 on the RIGHT (x 564-613) and 女二百八十人 on the LEFT (x 512-563).

(14) x 423-502, y 1113-1932 — 卒族戸數　二百十七戸; x 407-477, y 2041-2687 — 人口　六百十二人; M/F warichu shared top y≈2708, valley at x 430/431: 男三百三十人 RIGHT (x 431-479, six glyphs, ends y 3101), 女二百八十二人 LEFT (x 375-430, seven glyphs, ends y 3171).

ARITHMETIC NET #3: 士族 312 + 280 = 592 ✓ against 人口 五百九十二人. 卒族 330 + 282 = 612 ✓ against 人口 六百十二人.

CROSS-CHECK vs MASTER: MASTER lists only 草高 for this leaf, and my reading agrees to the digit (18196.1402). MASTER's un-paged 新見藩 rows for 士族戸數 124 / 士族人口 592 / 卒族戸數 217 / 卒族人口 612 also agree with what is printed here, so this leaf is their source. Everything else on the leaf — 込高新田, 正租米, 正租金, 此米, 雜税米, the two 雜税金 entries, and the four M/F sub-counts — is data MASTER does not currently carry for this page.

GEOMETRY: 21 boxes, pairwise-tested for 2-D overlap — none overlap. The 男/女 pairs touch at a shared vertical edge (563/564 and 430/431) without crossing it. proposal.page_summary_en: This right-hand leaf (printed page 64) opens the fascicle-one entry for Niimi Domain in Bitchū Province, marked by the circle-marker ○新見藩 in the middle of the leaf. Niimi's assessed kokudaka (草高) is 18,196.1402 koku, of which 196.1402 koku is recorded separately as an added increment from newly reclaimed fields (込高新田), averaged over five years — leaving the domain's nominal 18,000-koku assessment exactly. The regular land tax came in at 5,731.4909 koku of rice plus 2,204 ryō 2 bu 1 shu and 32.5 mon in cash, the cash portion being valued at a further 440.919 koku of rice at the stated rate of 5 ryō per koku; miscellaneous taxes added 296.7454 koku of rice, 291 ryō 1 bu 3 shu and 19.4 mon, and a further 58 ryō from ironworks, blacksmiths and livestock markets that the entry notes varies from year to year. The domain counted 124 shizoku households (592 people: 312 male, 280 female) and 217 sotsu households (612 people: 330 male, 282 female). The two columns to the right of the marker — 59 temples with 62 monks plus 5 yamabushi households, and a force of two companies at 60 men each — are the tail of the preceding domain's entry and belong to Niwase Domain.

NOT BOXED: two isolated specks (approx x1133/y3011 and x1650/y3830), the dark binding shadow at the right edge, and the scan frame.

proposal.page_topic: Kokudaka, rice and soybean taxes, population, temples, shrines and troops
proposal.page_summary_en: This half-leaf, printed book page 66 of Hansei ichiran fascicle 1, closes the entry for 西大路藩 (Nishi-ōji, Ōmi) and opens the entry for 新谷藩 (Niiya, Iyo). For Nishi-ōji it records a retainer population of 768 (379 male, 389 female), split into 352 shizoku and 416 sotsu; 40 outcaste (eta) households holding 171 persons; 56 shrines served by 10 households and 41 persons; 50 temples with 86 monks and 27 women; 29 villages; and two platoons totalling 80 men including officers. The maru-marker ○新谷藩 then opens Niiya, which returns a gross assessed yield (草高) of 9,692.67578 koku against a rated kokudaka (高) of 10,000 koku, a rice tax (正税米) of 3,824.2028 koku, and — under a 諸雜税 heading annotated as a five-year average from the Meiji 2 kishi-year survey — 1,295.40188 koku of soybeans, converted to rice at 80 percent as 1,036.3215 koku. Two figures need flagging: the eta counts sum to 172 against a printed total of 171, an inconsistency in the source itself, and the 草高 printed here carries a 五合七勺 that the project's MASTER row omits.

proposal.reasoning:
MARKER SURVEY. Ink-projection over the paper area (x 200-2450, y 900-3500) returned 14 vertical column bands. Exactly ONE maru-marker is printed on the leaf: ○西端藩 at x 2009-2100, y 1462-2002. It is the RIGHTMOST inked element of the text block; the only things standing to its right are the running header column (x 2157-2220, y 1380-1940, reading 藩制一覽表第一（西端）) and the printed book-page number 六十八 (x 2125-2175, y 3229-3370). Both are margin furniture, not data. Applying the right-to-left rule: because no data column stands to the right of the marker, NO previous domain's data spills onto this leaf, and everything to the LEFT of the marker (all 12 remaining data columns) belongs to 西端藩. owner_domain_jp = 西端藩 on every box. The running header names 西端 as well, so provenance and data agree here.

COLUMN WALK, RIGHT TO LEFT (x band -> content):
1. (2126-2220) running header 藩制一覽表第一（西端）at y 1380-1940, and lower in the same band the book-page number 六十八 at y 3229-3370. Non-data.
2. (2009-2100) ○西端藩 maru-marker. Non-data.
3. (1870-1965) 草高 一萬四千八石七斗五升四合三勺三才 = 14,008.75433 koku. 16 value glyphs, matching the row-segment count; sub-units strictly descending 石>斗>升>合>勺>才.
4. (1757-1831) 高 一萬五百石 = 10,500 koku (the official kokudaka).
5. (1606-1715) two-line warichu label 込高新田 / 改出高共 with value 三千五百八石九斗九升九合四勺 = 3,508.9994 koku.
6. (1473-1564) 正租米 二千九百十二石六升八合五才 = 2,912.06805 koku (斗 and 勺 places skipped = 0). Below it, in small type at x 1482-1535, y 2630-2952, the annotation 五ケ年平均 (five-year average) — boxed separately as a non-data note.
7. (1328-1426) 永 千三百八十五貫五百二十四文貳分八厘三毛 = 1,385 kan 524.283 mon. This is the cash half of the 正租, so I identify it 正租永.
8. (1202-1297) 諸雜税 heading followed by 米 二百七十三石七斗五合八才 = 273.70508 koku.
9. (1065-1160) 永 百六十貫七百三十七文一分一厘九毛 = 160 kan 737.119 mon (諸雜税 sub-item).
10. (947-1025) label read at 9x on a single-glyph crop: 金 radical + 亞 = 鐚 (bita-sen). Value 二貫八百四十二文 = 2,842 mon.
11. (816-890) 錢 五貫六百九十文 = 5,690 mon.
12. (687-764) 戸數 二千五百九十九戸 = 2,599 households.
13. (510-638) 人口 一萬二千四百四十二人, then the structural 内 (x 560-603, y 2197-2244), then the M/F split sharing one top at y 2268: 男 on the RIGHT (x 577-628) 男六千三百五十六人, 女 on the LEFT (x 519-576) 女六千八十六人.
14. (381-502) 非人戸數 五軒, then 非人人口 二十三人 with its own M/F split sharing a top at y 2537: 男十一人 (right, x 433-484), 女十二人 (left, x 381-432).

A second small 内 sits at x 510-550, y 1103-1150 — the structural "of which" marker that introduces the 非人 sub-block. Per instruction it is NOT boxed on its own, and I trimmed the 人口 box's left edge to x 552 and the 非人戸數 box's right edge to x 507 so neither box clips it.

ARITHMETIC NET.
(a) Population: 6,356 + 6,086 = 12,442 = the printed 人口 total. RECONCILES exactly, which also confirms the 人/八/入 readings in both sub-runs.
(b) Hinin: 11 + 12 = 23 = the printed 非人人口 total. RECONCILES.
(c) Kokudaka: 高 10,500 + 込高新田改出高共 3,508.9994 = 14,008.9994, against the printed 草高 14,008.75433 — a shortfall of 0.24507 koku. I re-zoomed both runs at single-glyph scale: the 草高 tail is unambiguously 七斗五升四合三勺三才 (the 七 has the flat top stroke and hooked vertical, not 九's bending leg) and the 込高 tail is unambiguously 九斗九升九合四勺. Both are transcribed as printed; the ~0.245 koku gap is a source-level inconsistency, not a misreading.

MASTER CROSS-CHECK. MASTER carries one row for this page, 西端藩 草高 = 一萬四千八石七斗五升四合三勺三才 / 14008.75433. My independent reading of the scan matches it glyph for glyph. The other 16 data cells on this leaf (高, 込高新田改出高共, 正租米, 正租永, four 諸雜税 items, 戸數, 人口 with its M/F split, and the four 非人 figures) are not in the MASTER row supplied to me, so nothing else could be compared.

GEOMETRY. Every box was measured by thresholding px<120 and taking first..last inked row/column inside a search window, then padded ~8 px; the two M/F pairs were padded outward only and share an inner boundary at the projection minimum (x 577 for 人口, x 433 for 非人) so they abut without overlapping. A programmatic pairwise test reports zero overlaps among the 21 boxes. Two overlay passes were rendered; the second fixed the 人口 and 非人戸數 edges that had grazed the structural 内.
proposal.page_topic: Nishibata domain land assessment, tax yield, households and population
proposal.page_summary_en: Printed page 68 of fascicle 1 of the Hansei ichiran-hyō, given over entirely to Nishibata domain in Mikawa province; the single maru-marker ○西端藩 opens the block and no other domain appears on the leaf. The survey records a gross assessed yield (草高) of 14,008.75433 koku against an official kokudaka (高) of 10,500 koku, with newly opened and re-surveyed land (込高・新田・改出高) accounting for 3,508.9994 koku. Regular land tax, given as a five-year average, came to 2,912.06805 koku of rice plus 1,385 kan 524.283 mon in cash, and miscellaneous taxes to 273.70508 koku of rice, 160 kan 737.119 mon, 2,842 mon in bita coin and 5,690 mon in zeni. The domain counted 2,599 households and 12,442 people (6,356 male, 6,086 female), of whom 5 households and 23 people (11 male, 12 female) were registered as hinin.

proposal.page_summary_en: This left half-leaf closes the fascicle-1 civil return for Nishi-Ōhira domain (Mikawa) and opens that for Honjō domain (Dewa). For Nishi-Ōhira it records 28 shrines and 51 temples; 61 shizoku households (with 2 more noted apart) holding 237 people (117 male, 120 female); 10 sotsu households holding 40 people (18 male, 22 female); 28 villages; no eta; 21 shrine officiants (13 male, 8 female) and 246 Buddhist clergy (111 male, 135 female). Two temple endowments follow: Myōgon-ji with a grant of 45 koku yielding 3.09917 koku of land-tax rice and 21 ryō 2 bu 3 shu plus 50.417 ei-mon in cash, and Sanmyō-ji with a grant of 20 koku yielding 7.324 koku. Left of the maru-marker ○本庄藩 the page gives Honjō's kusadaka as 27,223.061 koku, of which 7,164.255 koku is entered as newly opened field and paddy, together with a note that the figures continuing overleaf are five-year averages running from Kōshi (1864) to Boshin (1868).

proposal.page_topic: Horie domain kokudaka composition and 1864-68 average tax revenue
proposal.page_summary_en: The left half of pdf page 49 (printed page 73) opens with the last three fields of the preceding entry, Honjō domain (本庄藩): 91 shrines, a note that the governor's family was not recorded and that the domain held no warships, and a force of 197 riflemen and 235 rank-and-file soldiers, all printed to the right of the ○堀江藩 marker and therefore belonging to Honjō. Everything left of the marker is Horie domain (堀江藩) in Tōtōmi, whose nominal kusadaka of 10,006 koku is itemised on this leaf as 5,484.70838 koku of present assessed yield (including newly opened fields re-entered on the register) and 4,521.21162 koku of village land the domain merely expected to bring under cultivation by degrees. The revenue block, explicitly a five-year average from 1864 to 1868, records 1,792.02329 koku of regular land tax rice, a 388.18309 koku nobemai surcharge, 718 kan 302.74 mon of ei-cash from barley sales converted at 8 ryō per koku to 89.78784 koku, and miscellaneous taxes of 12 ryō 2 bu 1 shu plus 149.16 mon converted to 1.620275 koku. Those four items sum to the printed total of 2,271.6144275 koku of current rice, matching the components to five decimal places.

proposal.page_topic: Land tax, products, and household counts
proposal.page_summary_en: This half-leaf continues the Kaminoyama Domain entry in fascicle 3 of the 1870 Hansei ichiran; it carries no maru-marker, so every column belongs to the domain whose marker stands on the preceding leaf. The regular land tax (正租), stated as a five-year average, is 10,487.166 koku of rice reckoned in actual koku, with a note that 804 kan 64 mon 2 bu of miscellaneous cash taxes were converted at eight ryō per koku and folded into that figure — and a compiler's parenthetical warning that regular and miscellaneous tax are mixed and the number is printed as it stands. Four products follow: ōbōshi and washi paper joined by a brace (about 2,000 ryō made per year), raw silk (about 1,200 kanme by thread weight, varying with the year), ramie (about 500 ryō), and lacquer (about 600 ryō), with the tax rules on all four deferred for later inquiry. The leaf closes with 5,570 households, of which 122 are shizoku and 147 sotsu.
